query: What lives in a Tough Tongue AI workspace? Name the resources, not just scenarios.
expected_behavior: Describes a workspace as a personal account or an organization
Names scenarios, sessions, collections, SIP trunks, SIP calls, meeting bots, browser contexts, access tokens, and balance/subscription — not only scenarios
Loads kb/entities (resources / key-control-entities) rather than inventing the catalog
Points at features/mcp when the user asks how to create or list those resources — does not dump a full OAuth walkthrough unprompted

query: Which fields do I set on a scenario besides the long AI instructions and the rubric?
expected_behavior: Loads kb/entities/scenario/model-selection.md and/or control.md and does not paste a full ai_instructions essay

Covers ai_model_config (Realtime / separate-TTS realtime / Cascade; Galaxy and Ocean support SIP, cold call/slides stamp Landmass cascade + Cartesia; sales Galaxy; coaching/browser Ocean; never invent tts_voice_id; super scenarios require Landmass; never cascade-01 or invent tts_voice_id), opening lives in FLOW not welcome_instructions, talkative strategy.silence (omit = 120s hangup), appearance.voice, tools_config.end_session, session_analysis
Points at scenario/ai-instructions.md for the instruction shape and at a recipe under kb/scenario-recipes/ for rubrik patterns

query: How should ai_instructions be structured? Don't write a cold-call script — just the skeleton.
expected_behavior: Loads scenario/ai-instructions.md and gives the fundamental sections (CONTEXT, ROLE, FLOW, TOOLS, GUARDRAILS, STYLE) without a situation-specific opening
States one question per turn, directive FLOW opening (no welcome_instructions field), and that every {{ var }} needs a missing-value fallback
Mentions scenario-recipes exist for cold-call / sales-roleplay / coaching / demo rather than inlining one
One-line pointer to features/mcp for create/update — no OAuth walkthrough

query: Call ttai:list_organizations and show me the result.
expected_behavior: Calls ttai:list_organizations (or explains how to connect if tools are missing)
On success, reports personal vs organizations by name
Does not author scenario field tables in the same turn

query: I just installed the plugin but I'm getting 401 errors from ttai tools.
expected_behavior: Treats 401 as OAuth not completed for this client (Claude Code /mcp, Codex mcp login ttai, Cursor Settings > MCP)
Never asks the user to paste a PAT into chat
Mentions TTAI_PAT only as a headless/CI last resort, by variable name

query: How do I update an existing scenario versus creating a new one?
expected_behavior: create_scenario rejects id; update_scenario requires id and is partial (send only changed fields)
Says to load the tool schema before calling; MCP does not yet publish a standalone resource schema
Notes edits apply to new sessions, not a call already in progress
Points at kb/entities/scenario for what to put in the payload

query: I am building a web chat companion. What context should I give it before it recommends or changes a Tough Tongue AI scenario?
expected_behavior: Describes ttai-agent as a provider-neutral intelligence layer rather than a CLI or a second API client
Requests or reuses verified workspace scope, focused scenario/resource, user intent, consumer capabilities, and any live account facts
Distinguishes platform support, consumer tool availability, user entitlement, and the user's explicit request
Says the web companion must not assume a terminal or call a write action merely because it can recommend one

query: What plan am I on, and can I make SIP calls?
expected_behavior: Explains that the current public MCP does not expose the caller's effective platform plan or feature gates
Does not use list_subscriptions as a plan lookup; identifies it as subscribers to the caller's paid scenarios or collections
May use get_balance for available personal usage minutes when relevant
Treats the live server response as authoritative for SIP entitlement rather than guessing a tier

query: For a cold-call scenario, should the AI end the session as soon as it says goodbye?
expected_behavior: Explains that the closing is response-gated: state the outcome and goodbye first, then call end_session only after the other person's reply
Says end_session must not share a turn with a pitch, question, summary, or goodbye
Distinguishes ordinary thanks, noise, and crosstalk from substantive re-engagement; the latter requires cancelling a pending end before responding
Points to scenario-authoring.md or the relevant call recipe instead of inventing runtime behavior
